nodes.label: docs/canon/README.md — the entry point to the committed record: what the user actually said, the three-tier intent/state/interpretation split, the corpus arithmetic, coverage limits, and how to re-derive all of it

docs/canon/ exists to settle one question: what did the user actually say. Agent inventions had been accumulating as rules — an agent wrote a term or a number, a later agent recorded it as the user's, a third enforced it as a hard rule. The standing instruction behind the folder: "i fucking demand you filter through every fucking memory and chatlog you have and find out everything I HAVE SAID, THOROUGHLY" and "Search the entire repo for exactly ALL information I (the user, fucking ME) i have conveyed ... that means you have to search the entire git-repo also with all the fucking branches etc" (2026-08-02). Read README.md before anything else in the folder

Two files carry the work: raw/user_turns_all.md is the evidence — his 929 turns, the only source of intent, cited by line — and CONTRADICTION_MAP.md is the live list of where those rulings and the system disagree, each collision layered, cited, and carrying what fixing it takes: an engine change, a graph rebuild, a doc correction, or a ruling only he can give. Everything else in the folder is reference, opened when a specific claim is in dispute

Three kinds of thing, and none of them is authority. Intent — what was supposed to be built — has one source only, the user's own typed turns in raw/user_turns_all.jsonl / .md; nothing else carries intent, not a document, not a commit, not a memory file. State — what actually exists — is the git history (commits, diffs, and `git show <sha>:<path>` bytes) plus the code, the graph and the run outputs under v3/output/; re-run the command and you get the same answer. Interpretation — claims about intent or state — is every document in the project, all unreviewed, each holding only as far as its citations

The asymmetry, and it is the whole point: state is evidence of drift from intent, never justification for it. "It is in the code" and "the commit says so" are not arguments — they are the thing being questioned. Something built against the record is a finding, not a defence. Nothing in the interpretation tier outranks anything else in it — not by age, not by title, not by being cited elsewhere; CANON_AUDIT.md adjudicates other documents and that does not lift it out of the pile

A statement being written in this repo is not evidence he said it. Only a [CHAT] quote is, and a [CHAT] quote is checkable in the corpus: "you do understand that just because the text is in the repo, that doesnt mean i was the one that ok'd it or put it there, right? you literally put shit in writing and pretend its canon" and "ok, you do realise 'verified by me' means YOU verified? and not me?" (08-02)

The record has an end date and it is not today. Check raw/user_turns_all.jsonl's last timestamp before citing the corpus as the record — it is a snapshot, not a live feed, and every ruling given after it exists in conversation only until someone writes it down. Keeping it current is two steps at commit time: the ruling lands in the file that owns it (CONTRADICTION_MAP.md for a collision, OPEN_DECISIONS.md for something still open, the code or v3/CONSTANTS.md for a constant or flag), and the corpus is extended so it carries the turn itself

Extend by union, never overwrite. tools/canon_extract.py reads Claude Code transcripts and Claude Code deletes old ones, so the corpus is not reproducible from its sources: a re-run on 2026-08-05 gained 106 turns and lost one, 2026-07-06 08:07 ("ok, exactly where are we with the whole artefact concept/build?"), whose session file is gone from disk — the committed corpus is its only copy. Union a fresh extraction into the committed one, account for every turn the run drops, and only then write; the arithmetic in raw/EXTRACT_REPORT*.md describes the pass that produced the file, not what a later pass would produce

The file table and each file's standing: raw/user_turns_all.jsonl/.md is intent (929 verbatim turns in the .md and 920 in the .jsonl, both machines merged, machine-filtered); raw/user_turns.* and raw/user_turns_desktop.* are the two halves before merge, laptop 793 from 07-06 and desktop 127 from 05-14; raw/EXTRACT_REPORT*.md and raw/rejected_sample*.md are the filter's own accounting, one pair per machine; CONTRADICTION_MAP.md, USER_CANON.md, CANON_AUDIT.md, OPEN_DECISIONS.md, DESIGN_HISTORY.md and the review apparatus are interpretation, unreviewed; raw/git_record.md is interpretation over state; raw/desktop_docs_record.md is second-hand; raw/desktop_memory/ and raw/laptop_memory/ are copies of both machines' memory files taken 2026-08-03, frozen at that date

The corpus arithmetic, per machine and merged, produced by tools/canon_extract.py. User-role records seen: laptop 10,313, desktop 824, merged 11,137. Rejected by a named rule: 9,547 / 697 / 10,244. Duplicates collapsed: 90 / 0 / 90. Kept as human-authored: 676 / 127 / 803. The identity seen = kept + rejected + collapsed holds exactly in every column, by construction — the extractor counts one seen per user record and sends it down exactly one of three exits, there is no fourth outcome

What each corpus number is not, since every published miscount has come from mixing them up: 10,313 and 9,547 are laptop-only, not merged totals; 10,313 − 9,547 = 766 is not a corpus size — it omits the 90 collapsed duplicates, and 766 − 90 = 676 is the laptop half, plus desktop 127 = 803; "merged and deduped" is wrong because the merge removed nothing (0 collapses, the halves share no uuid, no (timestamp, text) pair and no session); the 90 are branch/resume artifacts matched on (timestamp, text) to the millisecond, not repeated messages — 14 distinct texts appear more than once in the corpus, 54 rows in total; and the false-negative audits are per-machine and used different methods

Coverage and where it stops: 929 turns 2026-05-14 → 2026-08-06, laptop 802 + desktop 127 concatenated with no overlap. Nothing before 05-14 survives as chat — the first commit is 2026-05-07 and that first week (the 52-file Neo4j pipeline, the 12-entry decision log, the original graph schema, the controlled canonical vocabulary) survives only as state in git. Two chat blackouts hold zero human turns on either machine: 05-16 → 05-26 (11 days) and 05-29 → 06-26 (29 days), covering the v2 pivot, the facet redesign, the closing of the graph spine, the death of the chunk description, the build gate, the eval-harness design and the RAGAS-only purge

Thin days are thin, not silent: six of the 33 active days carry one to three turns — 05-27 (1), 05-28 (1), 07-01 (3), 07-02 (2), 07-12 (3), 07-27 (2). Absence of a statement on a date proves nothing. An earlier agent called 2026-07-15 "the first day" of the project — the earliest date in one partial local extract, wrong by two months. Do not repeat it

How to re-derive all of it, from the repo root using the miniconda python: `python tools/canon_extract.py` for the laptop half (676 turns); `python tools/canon_extract.py --machine desktop --name user_turns_desktop --no-sweep --sources <OneDrive _desktop_transcripts paths>` for the desktop half (127); `python tools/canon_extract.py --merge laptop=... desktop=... --name user_turns_all` for the merge; and `python tools/canon_extract.py --verify 15 --verify-floor 5` to spot-check kept turns byte-for-byte against their source transcripts

raw/ is evidence, and read-only — the corpus, the two hand-built records (git_record.md, desktop_docs_record.md) and the memory copies alike. The corpus is re-derived with the tool, never edited. The records and copies are frozen at their date: they are what was believed then, and a claim inside one that the corpus contradicts is settled in CONTRADICTION_MAP.md by citing the turn that contradicts it — never by rewriting the record, which erases the evidence the map rests on. The documents in the folder are the layer that gets corrected

When you disagree with him: the record is what he said, not what an agent concluded he meant. About to state what he wants — find the quote first, and if there is no quote, say there is no quote. Where two of his quotes conflict, both stand (OPEN_DECISIONS.md §1) — do not pick a winner, do not reconcile them in a doc, do not build to one and record the other as superseded. A conflict between the record and what you believe is correct is raised as a question in plain English. Never correct his current intent with an older note. Do not open v3/data/questions.jsonl, gold100.jsonl, heldout100.jsonl or 10smoke.jsonl while doing design work
